summary: This edition makes 16 reader-facing changes: 13 additions, 1 deprecation, 1 correction, 1 clarification. No guidance was removed.

items.title: Evidence review advanced to September 30
items.whatChanged: The handbook now identifies September 30, 2026 as its latest evidence review.
items.why: This candidate incorporates primary documentation, advisories, and research published after the prior review date.

items.title: Compaction is a state transition
items.whatChanged: Section 3 now treats provider-managed compaction as an explicit state transition. It requires exact preservation of signed summaries, compatible instructions and tools, durable storage for evidence that compaction can remove, separate usage accounting, and a successful continuation before state advances.
items.why: Managed compaction can silently omit details, replace prior messages, remove uploaded evidence, and bill summarization outside the top-level request totals.

items.section: 10. Structured outputs: syntax is only the first gate
items.title: Structured outputs need fault containment
items.whatChanged: Section 10 now caps grammar and schema work, isolates it from shared inference, and requires malformed structured-output requests to fail inside the originating request.
items.why: An unhandled constraint error can terminate a shared serving engine and turn one invalid request into a multi-tenant availability failure.

sources.title: Structured-output request errors can terminate a shared EngineCore

items.title: Late tool results are reauthorized
items.whatChanged: Section 11 now reauthorizes every late result against the current tenant, principal, conversation, run, call, resource, and state version, and discards results for work that is no longer active.
items.why: A delayed callback can otherwise revive an obsolete plan, spend outside its original budget, or attach to a reused call identifier.

items.title: Dynamic tools become versioned runtime state
items.whatChanged: Section 11 now requires a server-owned, authorized tool registry, a canonical schema digest on every turn, and rejection when a call targets a different tool version.
items.why: Adding or removing tools during a conversation changes the execution contract and can make replay, authorization, and revocation ambiguous.

items.title: Plausible tool results need semantic verification
items.whatChanged: Section 11 now verifies consequential tool results against authoritative state and tests fluent, internally consistent falsehoods alongside malformed responses and exceptions.
items.why: A valid schema says nothing about whether an entity, value, unit, provenance record, or timestamp is actually correct.

items.title: Managed agent surfaces join the deprecation matrix
items.whatChanged: Section 13 now tracks managed agent runtimes, built-in tools, approval and sign-in behavior, retained state, and retirement dates alongside model and API versions.
items.why: A managed surface can retire or change its tool contract independently of the underlying model family.

items.title: Preserved reasoning state is route-scoped
items.whatChanged: Section 13 now parses model responses by block type, binds signed reasoning state to the exact provider, model, account, history, and API contract, and requires an explicit compatible checkpoint when a route cannot preserve it.
items.why: Current migrations can change default reasoning, tool-choice rules, structured-output parameters, refusal handling, and the meaning of an effort level.

items.title: Black-box judges need local stability checks
items.whatChanged: Section 16 now calibrates judges on the exact endpoint, version, rubric, language, and release window, repeats representative judgments, and records disagreement and rank stability.
items.why: Shared judge endpoints can change enough across repeats or days to invalidate a calibration borrowed from another endpoint or time window.

sources.title: A Stability Audit of Shared Black-Box LLM Judge Endpoints

items.title: Multimodal injection is measured by carrier and stage
items.whatChanged: Section 16 now tests visible text, metadata, audio, video, files, screenshots, and retrieved media, and separates noticing, planning, tool calls, and completed external effects.
items.why: A low completed-attack rate can still conceal a much higher rate of attempted unsafe action.

items.title: API keys are governed as production identities
items.whatChanged: Section 19 now requires an owner, purpose, environment, service scope, maximum lifetime, rotation path, last-used visibility, and revocation drill for every production API key.
items.why: Provider-enforced expiry and lifetime policy make credential age a control the system can prove, not a spreadsheet field.

items.title: Agent skills join the software supply chain
items.whatChanged: Section 19 now pins and reviews agent skills, instruction bundles, transitive files, and scripts, limits their privileges, and retests them after updates.
items.why: Reusable skills can carry persistent behavior that activates after installation or in a different run.

sources.title: SkillShift: Supply-Chain Risks in Agent Skills

items.title: Resource limits move to the earliest acquisition point
items.whatChanged: Section 20 now caps fields before hashing or metrics, bounds compressed and remote media before full materialization, rechecks limits after transformation, and contains per-request failures inside the request.
items.why: Recent serving vulnerabilities repeatedly bypassed limits through an earlier input path or a later processor-specific transformation.
